clue.text: Head north following soldier or saint

indicators.note: following tells us the head-north piece comes after the soldier, not before

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
to head somewhere is to go there
N is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A soldier marching north behind a saint, or a saint marching north behind a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head north' is two pieces, a verb and a direction, set after the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a model of excellence, and a saint is the classic figure of perfect virtue.

clue.text: Groovy instrument will fail test

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a farm implement that cuts furrows in soil
second meaning: old British student slang for failing an examination

explanation.walkthrough: 'Groovy' sounds like sixties slang, but it means making grooves. To plough an exam is dated British slang for failing it.
explanation.definitionFit: The farm tool makes grooves in the field, and to plough also means to flunk, as a verb in future sense with 'will'.

clue.text: Checked in — in a rush

indicators.note: the first in places the other word within the rush word

parts.note: a rush is a reed-like water plant
the second in taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller checked in at the airport in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like a hurry, but it is the marsh plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Reined, like a horse pulled back on its reins, means restrained or held back.

clue.text: Country worker, willing to be attendant

parts.note: game means willing, as in 'game for anything'
a keeper looks after something, an attendant

explanation.surface: A rural labourer keen to take a job as a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamekeeper is employed on a rural estate to rear and protect birds and animals for shooting.

clue.text: New woman, right? No way!

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
Eve, the first woman, is the crossword's stock woman
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A disbelieving reaction to news of a new woman in someone's life.
explanation.definitionFit: Never as an exclamation is an emphatic refusal or disbelief, the same as saying not a chance.

clue.text: Child in a bomb explosion

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so these letters land in a new order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A news report of a child caught up when a bomb went off.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambino is the Italian word for a baby or small child, borrowed into English.

clue.text: Detailed William to bring the Leica inside of the Houses of Parliament

indicators.note: inside places the photographic word within the shortened name
de-tailed means having its tail cut, so the final letter goes

parts.note: Bill is short for William; drop its last letter
Leica is a German brand of camera

explanation.surface: A reporter tells William to bring his camera inside Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'in detail' but is read as de-tailed: lose the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicameral means having two legislative chambers, as Parliament has the Commons and the Lords.

clue.text: Chain letters

definitions.meaning: first meaning: armour made of interlinked metal rings
second meaning: post delivered to your door

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'chain letters', the pass-it-on kind, but splits into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Chain mail is linked-ring armour, and post is called mail too, so the word covers both.

clue.text: Not doing much in Act IV at the end …

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the Roman numeral read as letters

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the

explanation.surface: A theatre critic notes an actor idle in the fourth act, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the following clue's overture for the surface story only.
explanation.definitionFit: Inactive describes someone idle, not taking action, which is doing little.

clue.text: … noted at the beginning

parts.note: surface reading: someone remarked at the start, continuing the previous clue
setter's reading: written in musical notes, a piece played at the start of an opera

explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' sounds like 'remarked on', but it means set to musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is the orchestral introduction played before an opera or ballet begins.

clue.text: Hate to follow first person on stage

indicators.note: only what follows the first letter is kept, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: a podium is a small raised stage a person stands on

explanation.surface: An actor dreading having to go on after the lead performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first letter of the platform word and what follows it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or loathing directed at someone, a formal synonym for hate.

clue.text: Do some needlework?

parts.note: surface reading: sew or embroider with a needle
setter's reading: work done with a hypodermic needle, giving a jab against disease

explanation.walkthrough: Needlework suggests sewing, but the needle here is a syringe.
explanation.definitionFit: To vaccinate is to inject a vaccine, typically with a syringe needle, to give immunity.

clue.text: Good play but nasty smell inside from the frogs possibly

indicators.note: inside says the smell sits within the play word, after the good

parts.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good
a reek is a strong unpleasant smell
a drama is a play

explanation.surface: A decent play spoiled by the stench of French cooking, the frogs being a slur for the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The frogs' looks like a jibe at the French, but it is The Frogs, a comedy by Aristophanes; 'possibly' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Frogs is a comedy by the ancient Athenian playwright Aristophanes, an instance of classical Greek theatre.

clue.text: Request to remain true to type

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Latin for 'let it stand', a plea that something stay

definitions.note: an instruction, not an adjective: keep the type as originally set
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the proofreader's mark telling the printer to keep the original text

explanation.surface: Someone asks a friend to stay just as they always are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'True to type' sounds like a personality, but type is printer's type.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is the proofreader's instruction to ignore a marked correction and leave the original wording in print.

clue.text: Indeed the monster had time to get dried out

parts.note: read as in deed: a deed is an act, and the in says what follows goes inside it
the Hydra is the many-headed monster of Greek myth
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone insists the mythical beast really did take ages to dry off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indeed' must be split: 'In deed', with the monster and time placed inside, the monster having the time after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dehydrated means having lost its water, which is to be dried out.

clue.text: Heard damn builder's keen to start

definitions.text: Heard damn builder's keen to start

indicators.note: to start puts the keen word at the front of the phrase

parts.note: keen means eager

indicators.note: heard means we go by sound, so the swearword stands for its soundalike

parts.note: damn spoken sounds like dam, and the animal famous for building dams is the beaver

explanation.surface: Someone overhears a building contractor swearing as he rushes to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a keen builder impatient to start.
explanation.definitionFit: An eager beaver is an idiom for an enthusiastic, hard-working person always keen to get on with the job.

clue.text: Will they provide protection in France from potential dangers surrounding me?

definitions.text: Will they provide protection in France

indicators.note: surrounding means the reordered letters go round the short pronoun
potential means the letters could become something else, so they are reordered

parts.note: the letters as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worried tourist asks who will keep them safe from threats in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Gendarmes are French armed police officers, whose job is public protection.

clue.text: Not on one of three sticks

definitions.text: Not on one of three sticks

parts.note: off is the opposite of on
a cricket wicket has three upright sticks called stumps

explanation.surface: Something that refuses to rest on any of three sticks.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the wicket has three upright sticks called stumps; the field is split into the on side and the off side, so the whole clue also defines the stump on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cricket term for the outermost of the three stumps, on the side away from the batsman's legs.

clue.text: Bewildering couple of fellows while baling out

indicators.note: while puts one thing during another, so the pair falls within the activity word

parts.note: baling out is scooping water from a boat
F is the abbreviation for fellow, so two of them

explanation.surface: Two men puzzled while scooping water out of a leaking boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Baffling means puzzling or confusing, something hard to understand.

clue.text: Son missing in transfer mix-up had friend who was like a brother

indicators.note: a mix-up throws things into a new order
missing tells us a letter is lost from the word before the mix

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, the letter to remove
taken as written
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A footballer's son was left out after a botched transfer, though a friend stood by him like a brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraternal comes from Latin frater, sibling; acting fraternally means behaving as a male sibling would.

clue.text: Discover the truth but don't start complaint

indicators.note: not starting means the opening letter is left off

parts.note: a grumble is a complaint

explanation.surface: Advice to find out what really happened without opening with a moan.
explanation.walkthrough: To rumble someone is informal British for to see through them or find them out.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumbling a plot or person means uncovering what is really going on, detecting the truth.

clue.text: These days lots of people are a market force

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the current era
a mass is a large crowd

explanation.surface: A commentator remarks that crowds of consumers now drive the economy.
explanation.walkthrough: AD is the label for years of the current era, so these days.
explanation.definitionFit: Admass is the mass public targeted by advertising, a consumer influence on what markets sell.

clue.text: Up to now having no right to a seat

indicators.note: having no right means the letter for right must be taken away

parts.note: so far means up to now
R is the abbreviation for right, the letter dropped

explanation.surface: Someone complains that they have not yet been entitled to a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is an upholstered seat for two or more people, so it is one kind of seat.

clue.text: Previous history of allotment at the rear

parts.note: at the back means at the rear
an allotment is a plot of ground rented for growing vegetables

explanation.surface: A local historian researching the past of a vegetable plot behind the houses.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a small rented garden plot in Britain; the rear piece comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's background is their past experience and circumstances, the history behind them.

clue.text: Either way it is a main form of transport

indicators.note: either way means the word reads the same in both directions

parts.note: the main is the sea, so a small craft that is paddled

explanation.surface: A claim that one mode of transport is the chief one whichever way you look at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like 'principal', but it is the old poetic word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A kayak is a small paddled boat, so it carries people over water.

clue.text: Odd flutter by old bird

indicators.note: to flutter is to flap about, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: the letters as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A strange flapping made by an ancient bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo was a flightless bird of Mauritius, hunted to extinction in the 1600s.

clue.text: In the same way, the prescribed dress's extremely lovely

parts.note: a uniform is clothing everyone is required to wear

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of lovely

explanation.surface: Praise for a school or regiment whose required outfit is lovely on everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniformly is an adverb meaning consistently, without variation, so everything is done alike.

clue.text: Sent back first-class fragment of bone

indicators.note: sent back means the combined letters are read from the end

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I
a bit is a small fragment

explanation.surface: An archaeologist returns a top-quality piece of bone to the museum.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a standard crossword way to get AI, the digit doubling as a letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger of the two bones in the lower leg.

clue.text: Glutton takes ages over the birds

indicators.note: in a down-style reading over puts the first piece above, so the glutton comes first

parts.note: a greedy eater is called a pig
eons are ages, very long periods

explanation.surface: A greedy eater spends ages over a dish of game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigeons are common birds of the dove family, so they are an example of birds.

clue.text: Children longing to go back inside for traditional breakfast dish

indicators.note: inside puts the backward word within the children word

parts.note: kids are children

indicators.note: to go back means the longing word is written backwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: Homesick children longing to go back for a proper cooked breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: Devilled kidneys were a staple of the old English country-house breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidneys, fried or devilled, are offal served in the traditional full English breakfast.
